mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has fallen in each of the last three weeks (-13.4 to -17.7), indicating continued reduction in commuting-linked errands and lunch-hour retail visits. This persistent decline should continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as the same behavioral pattern extends.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline or staying flat, indicating decoupling of workplace and retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses below -20 percent, it signals a critical reduction in public transit usage that constrains access to retail districts for transit-dependent populations, producing a sharp near-term drop in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or rises in the two weeks following a TRANSIT reading below -20, showing no transit-access dependency.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous week-over-week declines in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT compound each other: fewer people commuting by transit to workplaces reduces incidental retail stops along commute routes, producing a larger joint decline in RETAIL_REC than either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline for two consecutive weeks simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks is no larger than the decline predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, indicating no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated and rising PARKS mobility (44.9 to 51.9) indicates a seasonal shift toward outdoor recreation that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation activity, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks as consumers favor parks over shopping/dining venues.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 40 percent change from baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged above 44 for all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat while PARKS remains elevated above 40, indicating no substitution effect between parks and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GROCERY_PHARM (8.9 to 6.4), normally the most resilient category, suggests tightening policy restrictions or renewed caution that will soon spill over into discretionary RETAIL_REC mobility, driving it lower within one week as restrictions bite broadly.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 8.9 to 6.4 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week following three consecutive weekly drops in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained essentially flat near zero across all four weeks, indicating no new stay-at-home shift. This stability predicts a short-term stabilization or mild rebound in RETAIL_REC within one week as no new confinement behavior is emerging to suppress outside activity further.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 0.0 and 0.4 for four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next week despite RESIDENTIAL remaining flat, indicating residential stability does not predict retail stabilization.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's four-week decline (-12.1 to -13.7) is modest and decelerating in magnitude week-over-week, suggesting the downward trend is losing momentum and will mean-revert upward over the next four weeks as the initial shock dissipates.
evidence_refs: fact:week-over-week RETAIL_REC change shrank from -0.3 to +0.2
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline at the same or accelerating rate over the next 4 weeks rather than stabilizing or reversing.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling WORKPLACES and falling TRANSIT alongside falling GROCERY_PHARM signals a coordinated regime of renewed restrictions; when all three essential/commute categories decline together, discretionary RETAIL_REC mobility falls even more sharply within two weeks due to compounded policy-driven caution.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and GROCERY_PHARM all decline simultaneously for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline is not larger than historical baseline rate when all three series decline together, indicating no compounded policy effect.
